quote: Theorem. Let X1 and X2 be two independent random variables following the GTL−HT−G family of distributions with common parameters θ, b, ψ , and different shape parameters δ1 and δ2 , that is, X1 ∼ f1 (x; δ1 , θ, b, ψ) and X2 ∼ f2 (x; δ2 , θ, b, ψ). If δ1 > δ2 , then X1 and X2 are stochastically ordered.
family: Gamma Topp-Leone-Heavy Tailed-G (GTL−HT−G) family, pdf f(x; δ, b, θ, ψ) as in Eq. (4), δ, b, θ > 0, baseline parameter vector ψ
compared: shape parameter δ1 vs δ2; parameters θ, b, ψ common

hypotheses.text: Let X1 and X2 be two independent random variables following the GTL−HT−G family of distributions with common parameters θ, b, ψ , and different shape parameters δ1 and δ2
hypotheses.formal: X1 ~ f(.; δ1, θ, b, ψ), X2 ~ f(.; δ2, θ, b, ψ), X1 independent of X2

conclusion.direction: X1 <=lr X2 (f1/f2 non-increasing in x for δ1 > δ2, per proof); statement itself only says 'stochastically ordered'

quantifiers: δ1, δ2, b, θ > 0; all x in the common support
ambiguity: The statement concludes only that 'X1 and X2 are stochastically ordered' without naming an order or a direction; the proof shows d/dx[f1/f2] < 0 for δ1 > δ2 and asserts 'likelihood ratio order X ⪯lr Y exists', which formally gives X1 ⪯lr X2. In Eqs. (11) and the derivative the denominator is printed as f2 (x; δ1 , θ, b, ψ), a typo for δ2. Theorem is unnumbered.
